quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungary, September 9th traditionally marks the beginning of grape harvest season. Families would gather in vineyards to pick grapes for wine-making, often celebrating with music and feasts that lasted well into the evening.

short_read.title: The Secret Life of Garden Snails
short_read.teaser: These little gastropods can have over 14,000 teeth and navigate using two pairs of tentacles. Learn how these fascinating creatures help gardens thrive in surprising ways.

medium_read.title: The Ancient Forests of the Olympic Peninsula
medium_read.teaser: Massive Sitka spruce and western red cedars in the Olympic rainforest can live over 500 years. Discover how these gentle giants create entire ecosystems in their branches.

long_read.title: The Women Who Mapped the Ocean Floor
long_read.teaser: Marie Tharp's hand-drawn maps in the 1950s revealed underwater mountain ranges and changed our understanding of Earth. Her detective work proved continents actually move, revolutionizing geology.

port_angeles.title: Bald Eagle Season Begins
port_angeles.description: September marks the return of bald eagles to the Strait of Juan de Fuca for salmon season. Over the next few months, dozens of these magnificent birds gather along the shoreline, and Ediz Hook is one of the best spots to watch them fish and soar.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! You know your hummingbird facts! Their tiny hearts beat incredibly fast to power those rapid wings.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! These tiny birds have hearts that beat about 1,200 times per minute — that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These remarkable little birds have hearts that beat about 1,200 times per minute while flying! That's what powers their incredible hovering ability.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To compare, a human heart beats about 60-100 times per minute at rest. Hummingbirds need this rapid heartbeat to fuel their unique ability to hover and fly backwards.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Gyönyörű! That's right — pillangó is butterfly in Hungarian! Such a lovely, musical word.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound beautiful? Virág means flower, madár means bird, and csillag means star.
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The word 'pillangó' may come from an old Hungarian word meaning 'fluttering one.' Hungary is home to over 200 species of butterflies, including the stunning swallowtails.

puzzle_3.question: What tree produces the largest seed cones in the world?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! The Coulter pine produces massive cones that can weigh up to 10 pounds — they're sometimes called 'widowmakers' because they're so heavy!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's actually the Coulter pine! These California natives produce enormous cones weighing up to 10 pounds with thick, sharp scales.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Coulter pine cones can measure over a foot long and are armed with sharp, curved spines. They're found in the mountains of Southern California and northern Baja California.
